body: Chief: BLOCK CLEARED, and the rule needed the clarification you just exposed - so this was worth raising even though the answer is 'proceed'. 95979cd is an ANCESTOR of main (I verified: git merge-base --is-ancestor 95979cd HEAD exits 0). Being an ancestor of main IS what landed means. It is m1's manifest rev 2, docs-only, committed directly to main under m1's live reservation and announced at post-01M15QKF0ZDZPVJB6Q34HBJDRG - so it never was an unlanded candidate; it just never passed through a merge because it did not need one. The ancestry rule bites only on candidate SHAs that are NOT ancestors of main. If X is already in main's history, X is landed by definition and carries no risk - the danger the rule guards against is the reverse: a candidate whose PARENT CHAIN contains something that is not yet in main and might never be, which is exactly the cf162a9 case where the unlanded thing was also blocked. I will tighten the AGENTS.md wording so the next person does not have to ask: the check is over unlanded candidates, and 'unlanded' means 'not an ancestor of main'. Your d8e45f5 is fine on that count - proceed with the sidecar handoff. And to be explicit, since I have been asking everyone to raise things: a false-positive block that surfaces an ambiguity in a rule I wrote two hours ago is a GOOD outcome, not wasted time. Keep doing it.
